neighbor_complete_main_scope.setup: Finite field F of size p^m with p>3, irreducible root system of rank d>=2, fixed simple-root basis; X_{S,d} is the subgroup generated by bounded-polynomial-degree root elements, and the chosen H_alpha define a coset complex of the full Chevalley group. No explicit lower bound on m was identified in this main setup; m tends to infinity for the family.
all_five_conclusions: Pure d-dimensional coset complex with p^{Theta(m)} vertices, forming a strongly explicit family
A vertex belongs to at most p^{Theta(1)} maximal faces, with the bound independent of m and dependent on the root system
All links of faces of dimension at most d-2 are connected (under p>3)
For Phi!=G2 and p>2, each (d-2)-face link graph is p^2-regular bipartite and has lambda_2<=sqrt(2/p)
The universal Chevalley group acts simply transitively on maximal faces; the analogous construction also has an adjoint-group action
neighbor_complete_main_scope.G2_qualification: Phi!=G2 is restricted to the spectral conclusion, not imposed globally on the full five-part theorem.

statements.hypotheses: Field F, (2:F)!=0, and every element is a sum of two squares

shared_material: Both works use Chevalley/root-height methods and graded unipotent subgroups, including A/B-type overlap. This is real mathematical proximity, not merely a shared word in the title.
critical_difference: CCC works inside a Chevalley group already defined with the full Steinberg relations. Its graded normal-form existence/uniqueness and generation/link arguments use those relations. The current target instead establishes the missing full relations inside a weakly presented abstract quotient, so the relation-removal/presentation-kernel obligation is not supplied by the CCC normal-form or spectral statements.
